title_en: Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Enforcement of Mortgaged Houses by the People's Courts

articles.content_en: Article 1: For a house owned by the person subject to enforcement that has been lawfully mortgaged, the People's Court may seal it up, and may, upon application of the mortgagee, auction, sell off, or set off the debt according to law.

Article 2: Where the People's Court, in respect of a house already lawfully mortgaged that is inhabited by the person subject to enforcement and the family members he/she supports, after ruling for auction, sell off, or set off the debt, shall grant the person subject to enforcement a grace period of six months. Within this period, the person subject to enforcement shall voluntarily vacate the house, and the People's Court shall not forcibly remove the person subject to enforcement and the family members he/she supports from the house.

Article 3: After the expiration of the aforesaid grace period, if the person subject to enforcement has not yet moved out, the People's Court may render a ruling for forcible removal and shall enforce it in accordance with Article 229 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China.
At the time of forcible removal, if the person subject to enforcement is unable to resolve the housing problem on his/her own, upon verification by the People's Court, the person applying for enforcement may provide temporary housing to the person subject to enforcement and the family members he/she supports.

Article 4: The temporary housing provided by the person applying for enforcement may have a different quality and location from the person's original housing, and the area shall be determined by reference to the per capita floor area standard for low-rent housing prescribed in the "Administrative Measures for Low-Rent Housing for the Lowest-Income Families in Urban Areas" jointly issued by the Ministry of Construction, the Ministry of Finance, the Ministry of Civil Affairs, the Ministry of Land and Resources, and the State Administration of Taxation.

Article 5: The temporary housing provided by the person applying for enforcement shall be subject to rent. The rent standard shall be determined through negotiation between the person applying for enforcement and the person subject to enforcement; if negotiation fails, it shall be determined by the People's Court by reference to the rent standard for similar local houses, and if there is no rent standard for similar local houses for reference, it shall be determined by reference to the average rent standard in the local housing rental market.
The rent that has already accrued may be deducted in priority from the proceeds from the auction or sell-off of the house.

Article 6: If the person subject to enforcement is a recipient of subsistence allowances and is unable to resolve the housing problem on his/her own, the People's Court shall not forcibly remove him/her.

Article 7: These Provisions shall come into force as of the date of promulgation. Where any judicial interpretation previously published by this Court before the coming into force is inconsistent with these Provisions, these Provisions shall prevail.
December 14, 2005.
